Build a subset connectivity report (preferred alias)

Source: R/api-reports.R
subset_connectivity_report.Rd

Build a subset connectivity report (preferred alias)

Usage

subset_connectivity_report(
  fit = NULL,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  top_n_subsets = NULL,
  min_observations = 0,
  data = NULL,
  person = NULL,
  facets = NULL,
  score = NULL,
  basis = c("observed", "planned"),
  weight = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm().

top_n_subsets

Optional maximum number of subset rows to keep.

min_observations

Minimum observations required to keep a subset row.

data

Optional raw assignment/rating data, supplied instead of fit.

person, facets

Names of the person column and one or more facet columns in data. Include only Rater in facets to inspect person-rater links without a common Criterion node obscuring separate panels.

score

Numeric score column for basis = "observed". Recode study-specific missing markers to NA first; no category recoding or estimation is done.

basis

"observed" includes rows with complete identifiers and nonmissing finite scores; "planned" includes complete assignment rows without scores. Planned networks require score = NULL and weight = NULL.

weight

Optional numeric weight column for observed raw data. Missing and zero-weight rows do not create edges. Edge weights still count rows, not sampling weights. Negative or infinite weights are refused.

Value

A named list with subset-connectivity components. Class: mfrm_subset_connectivity.

Details

summary(out) is supported through summary(). plot(out) is dispatched through plot() for class mfrm_subset_connectivity (type = "subset_observations", "facet_levels", or "linking_matrix" / "coverage_matrix" / "design_matrix" / "network"). The network route returns reusable node and edge tables with draw = FALSE; drawing uses igraph when available.

Interpreting output

  • summary: number and size of connected subsets.

  • subset table: whether data are fragmented into disconnected components.

  • facet-level columns: where connectivity bottlenecks occur.

Typical workflow

  1. Run subset_connectivity_report(fit).

  2. Inspect graph coverage alongside identification_audit. A common criterion can connect panels whose person/rater locations remain confounded.

  3. Use the model rank and population assumptions to assess linking; a single co-observation component is not a FACETS identification subset.

Before fitting

Supply data, person, facets and score instead of fit. Known levels from incomplete/unscored rows remain as nodes, including isolates. A planned assignment roster can be examined with basis = "planned"; absent assignments cannot be reconstructed from an observed-only file. row_usage records each input row's inclusion and first exclusion reason. With a fit, only its retained rows are available here; review original missing assignments before fitting. No prefit result supplies an identification audit or model-readiness decision. settings$is_disjoint describes the source graph, even when subset filters omit components; compare source/retained subset counts. Filters do not establish linking. See online networks and reporting guide for a panel example.

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), mfrm_network_analysis(), measurable_summary_table(), data_quality_report(), mfrmr_linking_and_dff, mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

# Supplementary workflow: run explicitly to keep routine checks brief.
# example("subset_connectivity_report", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
out <- subset_connectivity_report(fit)
summary(out)
p_sub <- plot(out, draw = FALSE)
p_design <- plot(out, type = "design_matrix", draw = FALSE)
p_net <- plot(out, type = "network", draw = FALSE)
p_sub$data$plot
p_design$data$plot
p_net$data$edges
out$summary[, c("Subset", "Observations", "ObservationPercent")]
} # }
